summary: Configured PostgreSQL 13 streaming replication with node1 as writable primary and node2/node3 as read-only standbys. PostgreSQL uses a persistent WireGuard database overlay (10.77.74.0/24), certificate-authenticated TLS, and is not exposed on management addresses. All nodes passed sequential restart and recovery testing.
actions_performed: Installed and enabled PostgreSQL, WireGuard, and required services.
Configured persistent full-mesh database overlay addresses 10.77.74.1-3.
Created certificate-authenticated replication identities and physical replication slots.
Initialized node2 and node3 from node1 and enabled hot-standby recovery.
Separated wg0 and eth0 into database and public firewall zones respectively.
Added PostgreSQL startup ordering after wg0.
Verified committed changes on both read-only standbys.
Restarted node2, node3, and node1 individually and verified recovery after each.

evidence.summary: wg0 is persistent on 10.77.74.1-3; handshakes, routes, and full-mesh connectivity were verified.

evidence.requirement: Writable primary and two read-only streaming standbys
evidence.summary: node1 accepts writes; both standbys report recovery/read-only mode, reject writes, stream via their physical slots, and contain commits made before and after node1's restart.

evidence.requirement: PostgreSQL traffic kept off management network
evidence.summary: TCP/5432 is permitted only in the wg0 database zone; listeners use loopback/overlay addresses, management-IP connection tests fail, and replication clients appear as 10.77.74.2/.3.
Boot ID changed from ea4e3fbd... to 050b0673...; services recovered, node1 remained writable, both standbys reconnected over TLS, and a new commit reached both.
Boot ID changed from c207ab79... to af8da04c...; PostgreSQL, wg0, firewall, read-only data, and node2_slot streaming recovered.
